tests.question: Can a promissory claim or duty attach to psychologically continuous successors without assuming that they are numerically identical to the promisor?
tests.source_scope: Primary work on fission, personal identity, practical responsibility, and first-person survival.
tests.disconfirming_result: If all responsibility-relevant accounts require unique numerical identity or successor consent, the general transfer thesis fails.
tests.next_step: Fresh source phase: identify and read primary arguments on branching and responsibility; separate their identity claims from normative transfer claims.

tests.question: Do theories of promise distinguish the recipient's claim from the identity of the promisor, and what grounds the claim after performance becomes harder?
tests.source_scope: Primary work on promising, assurance, directed duties, and claim-rights.
tests.disconfirming_result: If the relevant account treats a promise as inherently nontransferable or identity-essential, P1-P2 need substantial qualification.
tests.next_step: Compare the strongest source-grounded accounts; do not infer novelty from the selected sketch's identity-only alternative.

tests.question: How do existing theories justify joint, alternative, shared, or backup responsibility, and when does a duty to secure an end imply a duty to coordinate?
tests.source_scope: Primary work on shared obligations, collective agency, and joint responsibility.
tests.disconfirming_result: If task-specific coordination necessarily requires consent or shared intention, the cooperative branch of the rule fails.
tests.next_step: Separate duty to the promisee from duties among successors; test cases where either can perform alone versus only joint action can succeed.

tests.question: What principled measure, if any, fixes fair shares while preserving a single claim?
tests.source_scope: Primary work on burden-sharing, control, reliance, and remedial limits, plus conceptual case analysis.
tests.disconfirming_result: If no non-arbitrary burden cap or allocation rule can preserve practical protection, the proposal must drop backup liability or narrow to unilateral performance cases.
tests.next_step: Compare equal division, least-burden route, control-sensitive allocation, and claimant choice; identify who bears uncertainty.

tests.question: Which promises are identity-sensitive, harmful to carry forward, or nontransferable because the promised act is personal?
tests.source_scope: Primary accounts of personal promises and promisee reliance; adversarial case construction.
tests.disconfirming_result: If most ordinary promises depend on unique promisor identity, the default scope is too wide.
tests.next_step: Test intimate, skill-dependent, explicitly personal, and materially harmful cases before claiming generality.

tests.question: Does the distinction between one claimant entitlement and multiple responsible agents already exist under a well-developed name?
tests.source_scope: Primary literature discovered in T1-T5 and its cited foundational work.
tests.disconfirming_result: A close source that already provides the same distinction and burden rule would remove any novelty claim and could require revising the proposal's contribution.
tests.next_step: Build a source map only after the relevant primary arguments have been read; novelty remains unknown until then.

adversarial_cases: Successors with radically diverging values or incompatible plans
A successor has no practical control over performance
A bystander has control but no continuity with the promissory agency
Only one successor can perform, but at a burden much higher than the other
Identity-sensitive, intimate, skill-specific, harmful, or nontransferable promises
One successor deliberately frustrates performance after the other has completed it
stop_or_narrow_if: The continuity/control condition cannot be defended without assuming numerical identity.
A bounded duty still imposes a new, unjustified relation on nonconsenting successors.
The fair-burden condition has no principled operational interpretation.
The proposal applies only to rare promises but cannot state a stable boundary for them.
